item.title: Gold Holds Gain Above $4,100 as Lower Oil Eases Inflation Woes
item.description: Gold held gains as inflation concerns eased alongside oil prices on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Japan’s Household Spending Slumps Most Since Pandemic
item.description: Japan’s household spending unexpectedly fell by the most since 2020, highlighting persistent weakness in consumption, even as the Bank of Japan grows more confident that inflation has become entrenched enough to warrant further interest-rate increases.

item.title: ExxonMobil Signs Deal in Step Toward Re-Entering Venezuela
item.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. formalized negotiations with Venezuela about operating one or more oil fields, months after Chief Executive Officer Darren Woods called the country “uninvestable” given its condition at the time.

item.title: Baltic Exchange's Oil Benchmark TD3C Described as `Complete Nonsense'
item.description: Legal filings and testimony provide a glimpse into tensions at the Baltic Exchange, which sets benchmark prices for shipping commodities.

item.title: Banxico Chief Signals No Rush to Cut Again After Surprise Move
item.description: Mexico’s surprise interest rate cut was a one-time move rather than the start of an extended easing cycle, Central Bank Governor Victoria Rodríguez said in an interview.
